# Homeostat

> Homeostat is a self-hosted health data vault. WHOOP, Garmin and FreeStyle Libre data go into one SQLite file on your own computer. A local daemon on 127.0.0.1 is the only writer, and every value links to the raw record it came from.

Homeostat is an early preview. It runs from source today and there is no installer yet. A public live demo at https://demo.gethomeostat.com runs the real app on synthetic sample data: read-only, no sign-up, and questions are answered by Claude up to a daily limit. The source repository is private; a source release is coming, under the MIT license.

What it does:

- Imports WHOOP, Garmin and FreeStyle Libre data into one local SQLite database.
- Shows the evidence behind every value: connector, batch, raw payload hash and revision.
- Ask: plain-language questions with cited answers, from Claude on the user's own Anthropic API key. Only the question and the records it needs go to Anthropic. Ollama is optional: it runs locally, needs no key, and nothing leaves the machine.
- MCP server for your own agents, FHIR R4 export, offline run maps from a local PMTiles basemap, a Training page and Goals.
- Stored secrets, including the Anthropic API key, are encrypted with AES-256-GCM in the local vault. No account and no telemetry. The only Homeostat server is the public demo, which holds synthetic data.

Homeostat is not a medical device and gives no medical advice. Screenshots on the site show synthetic sample data.
